question.text: The SEBI Master Circular is updated:

answer.text: Periodically to consolidate all existing circulars and incorporate new regulatory requirements
Never, as the original circular remains unchanged
Only when a new exchange is established

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's practice is to update Master Circulars periodically — typically on an annual or as-needed basis — so that they consolidate all previously issued circulars on the subject and incorporate new regulatory requirements as they emerge. This avoids the proliferation of standalone circulars and gives the industry a single, current reference for compliance. The Trap: Master Circulars are not frozen permanently, are not refreshed only once every 10 years, and are not updated only when a new exchange is established. Their core purpose is periodic consolidation and refreshing. Note: The periodic-consolidation update mechanism for SEBI Master Circulars is not described in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages only refer to individual circulars and one Master Circular contract-size reference. The framing above reflects general SEBI regulatory-practice knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
